title: AI-Mediated Marketing Myopia: How Algorithmic Governance Reshapes Customer-Centricity and Human Agency
content: AI ostensibly creates tension among customer-centricity, human agency, and stakeholders. This integrative literature review examines how AI is conceptualized in marketing and whether algorithmic governance and new marketing myopia explain how AI-mediated marketing narrows organizational attention to customers at the expense of human agents and other stakeholders. Searches of Google Scholar and ScienceDirect yielded 107 studies. Following PRISMA 2020, 38 studies were ultimately analyzed. The findings indicate that AI is framed as a performance instrument whose outcomes depend on organizational and human capabilities. AI-mediated marketing shifts customer-centricity from experienced understanding toward measurable representation and risks turning delegation into substitution of human agency. The review derives five socio-technical mechanisms through which algorithmic governance conditions may narrow customer value, customer understanding, and stakeholder responsibility: metric capture, datafied objectification, opacity-driven deference, accountability displacement, and agency substitution. These mechanisms are theoretically derived propositions for empirical testing, not tested causal relationships. This study contributes an integrated framework locating myopia in governance conditions rather than in AI itself.
